The cost of installation and upkeep far exceeds what you save on power, whereas a "normal" panel (like in a rooftop setup) will generate more power and cost less to configure. Plus you can't really just "store" power out on country roads and then deliver back to the towns where the power is actually used. The handful of potential advantages don't really pan out, either. Viewing LEDs at a low angle makes them very hard to see, so they'd have to be very bright, which takes a huge cut in the power generated (plus you almost can't see them at all during the day). Heating them drains power, too, while making the cells less effective.
